Task: Develop a complete lesson plan for teaching probability to high-school students.

Comprehensive Lesson Plan  
Subject: Mathematics – Probability  
Grade Level: High School (Grades 9-10, adaptable 8-12)  
Duration: One 90-minute block OR two 45-minute periods  

----------------------------------------------------
1. Standards Alignment (USA – Common Core & NCTM)
• CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS-CP.A.1   (Understand probability in terms of sample spaces)  
• CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSS-CP.A.2   (Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions)  
• CCSS.MATH.PRACTICE.MP2, MP4, MP5 (Reason abstractly, model, use tools)  
• NCTM Principles & Standards: Data Analysis & Probability (Grades 9-12)

----------------------------------------------------
2. Learning Objectives (SWBAT…)
1. Define and distinguish theoretical vs. experimental probability.  
2. Construct a sample space for a simple event (coin, die, spinner, cards).  
3. Calculate the probability of a single event using P(E)=# favorable/# total.  
4. Recognize complementary events and verify P(E)+P(E′)=1.  
5. Compare experimental results to theoretical expectations and explain discrepancies.  
6. Communicate probability reasoning verbally, visually, and algebraically.

----------------------------------------------------
3. Materials & Technology
• 30 coins, 15 six-sided dice, 6 colored spinners, 1 deck of playing cards per group  
• Chart paper or whiteboards & markers  
• Sticky notes (exit tickets)  
• Student devices (phones, tablets, or laptops) with internet OR teacher computer + projector  
• Online simulators: “Random Org Dice,” “Math is Fun Spinner,” or Desmos Probability Sim  
• Printable worksheets (guided & independent practice)  
• “Probability Lab Sheet” (data-table template)  

----------------------------------------------------
4. Vocabulary
Probability, experiment, outcome, sample space, event, favorable, theoretical, experimental (empirical), complement, relative frequency.

----------------------------------------------------
5. Lesson Sequence

A. Warm-Up / Hook (10 min)  
• Slide shows a single question: “Predict—if we flip a fair coin 20 times, how many heads will appear?”  
• Students record individual predictions on sticky notes and post them on a number line from 0-20 at front. Quick discussion highlights variation and introduces uncertainty.

B. Direct Instruction & Interactive Notes (20 min)  
1. Definition of probability; introduce notation P(E).  
2. Constructing a sample space (e.g., {H,T}).  
3. Formula P(E)=favorable outcomes ÷ total outcomes; emphasize 0 ≤ P ≤ 1.  
4. Complement rule.  
• Teacher utilizes real-time Desmos simulator to illustrate large-sample coin flips.

C. Guided Practice – “Mini-Lab Stations” (30 min)  
(Students in groups of 3-4 rotate every 10 minutes.)  
Station 1: 20 coin tosses → record heads count.  
Station 2: 30 dice rolls → record each face frequency; compute P(rolling 6).  
Station 3: Spinner with 4 colors (unequal sectors) → 25 spins; compute empirical probabilities.  
• At each station students fill “Probability Lab Sheet”: sample space, theoretical P, experimental P, % error.

D. Mid-Lesson Check (Formative) (5 min)  
• Teacher circulates, asks each group “Which station’s experimental result is closest to theoretical? Why might others differ?”

E. Consolidation / Discussion (10 min)  
• Groups post bar graphs of theoretical vs experimental results on board.  
• Whole-class debrief: Law of Large Numbers idea (qualitative), role of randomness.

F. Independent Practice (10 min)  
Worksheet (varied difficulty) – problems include:  
1. Card probabilities (e.g., P(drawing a heart)).  
2. Complement questions (P(not ace)).  
3. Contextual word problem (rain forecast).  
• Teacher offers scaffolds (vocabulary bank, sentence frames).

G. Closure / Exit Ticket (5 min)  
On a sticky note students answer:  
Q1 – Define experimental probability in your own words.  
Q2 – If P(E)=0.25, what is P(E′)?  

----------------------------------------------------
6. Assessment
Formative: Warm-up predictions, lab data accuracy, teacher questioning, mid-lesson check.  
Summative: Independent-practice worksheet (graded), exit ticket (2 pts).  

----------------------------------------------------
7. Differentiation & UDL
• Multimodal: tactile (coins/dice), visual (graphs), auditory (discussion), digital simulations.  
• ELL supports: word wall, sentence frames (“The probability of … is … because…”), visuals.  
• SPED: reduced-number data trials, peer buddy, calculator option.  
• Advanced: optional extension task (compound probability or two-way tables).  

----------------------------------------------------
8. Homework / Extension (choose one)
a) “Household Probability”: Students design and perform a 50-trial experiment at home (e.g., coin, spinner app) and write a short reflection comparing results to theory.  
b) Challenge: Calculate probability of drawing 2 red marbles without replacement from a bag containing 5 red and 7 blue.  

----------------------------------------------------
9. Cross-Curricular & Real-Life Connections
• Science (genetics – Punnett squares as probability).  
• Social studies (election polling margins).  
• Sports analytics (free-throw percentages).  
• Economics (insurance risk).  

----------------------------------------------------
10. Teacher Reflection (post-lesson)
• Were objectives met? Evidence from exit tickets.  
• Which station engaged students most?  
• Adjust pacing or group size?  
• Plan follow-up: Introduce compound events and independent/dependent probability next class.

----------------------------------------------------
11. Optional Day-2 Extensions (if splitting block)
Period 1 = Sections A-C; Period 2 = Sections D-G plus introduction to compound events with two-way tables or tree diagrams.

----------------------------------------------------
12. Printable / Digital Resources (links suggested)
• Desmos Probability Sim: https://teacher.desmos.com/activitybuilder (search “Marbleslides: Probability”)  
• PhET “Plinko Probability”: https://phet.colorado.edu/en/simulations/plinko-probability  
• OpenMiddle Probability Problems (rigor & depth).  

This plan equips teachers with objectives, activities, assessments, differentiation, and extensions to foster deep, hands-on understanding of foundational probability concepts for high-school learners.
